content: Is there any reason why we might not want to put a MeasureSpace instance on docs#Metric.sphere using docs#MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere ? (source of the problem: I tried #synth and it didn't work)
Would you care to explain why not? Just out of curiosity.
Perhaps because volume.toSphere is a constant factor away from the surface area that one might expect? (or one might expect whole sphere = 1 but this isn't either) sorry I didn't read carefully

Joris van Winden said:

Would you care to explain why not? Just out of curiosity.

Actually, now that I think about it more, I don't know. My initial idea was that it would upset the probabilists, but then again the same argument could be applied to the Lebesgue measure on R\mathbb{R}R. So consider the question still open. @Weiyi Wang I think the factor is correct, no? Maybe we can tag @Yury G. Kudryashov since he's the author.

I think maybe the issue could be the subtyping? But this is a very specific subtype, not a generic one, so I am not sure the argument applies.
That's why I crossed out my message
